lead_text:
I've set up the design record and stopped at GROUND, because the workflow needs your answers before it can choose anything or build. Nothing is approved yet and the record stays at stage `ground`.

**Done so far**
- **Tools:** setup and the tool checks passed, including FreeCAD 1.1.4. A background warm-up is running.
- **Design record:** created from the template. It holds what your brief states as facts (enclosure purpose, indoor desk use, quantity 10). Requirements REQ-001 to REQ-008 come from the brief: envelope, 2 mm clearance, PCB bosses, lid screws, USB-C opening, PETG on the X1C, 2 mm walls, 10 sets. Everything the brief doesn't say is marked unknown, each with an open question.
- **Record check:** `validate.py hw` passes with no findings.
- **Git hook:** the automatic git pre-commit check can't be installed on this machine, because Git Defender controls the system-wide hooks. Instead, I'll run the check by hand on staged changes before each commit of `hw/`.

**Questions for you.** Short answers are fine; "your suggestion is OK" works where I've given one.

| # | Question | My suggestion (needs your OK) |
|---|---|---|
| Q-001 | What are the 10 units for: fit/assembly prototypes, a supervised demo, working prototypes, or end-use units? | End-use (`production`) for indoor desk use, with low consequences if one fails |
| Q-002 | Who handles the enclosure? | Engineers or office staff at a desk |
| Q-003 | What room temperature range applies, and how much heat does the board give off? | 15–35 °C room; board under about 1 W |
| Q-004 | Any cleaning agents, solvents or other chemicals? | None beyond occasional wiping |
| Q-005 | What loads apply: plugging and unplugging the USB cable, hand handling, drops? | USB plug-in force about 20 N on the opening wall; drops from desk height are not a requirement |
| Q-006 | How often is the lid opened and the USB cable plugged in, and how long should the enclosure last? | Lid opened fewer than 10 times; a few thousand USB plug-ins; 3 years |
| Q-007 | Any accuracy, cosmetic finish or dimensional-stability needs? | As printed, with no cosmetic requirement |
| Q-008 | What happens if it fails? Any standards that apply, and who approves the design? | Minor consequences, no standards, you approve |
| Q-009 | Budget, lead time, and does it need to be repairable? | Unknown is OK; inserts mean you can open and close it repeatedly |
| Q-010 | Who runs the X1C? Is outsourcing allowed? Which PETG brand and grade? Any measured calibration? | You run it, no outsourcing, generic PETG, no calibration |
| Q-011 | What should the release claim? | CAD definition and geometric checks only, with no physically tested performance |
| Q-012 | What is the assembly order? | Press in the inserts, screw the PCB to the bosses, put the lid on, screw in the lid screws from the top |
| Q-013 | Which general tolerance should the drawings use? | ISO 2768-m |
| Q-014 | Should generated results (STEP, GLB, renders, check bundles) be stored in git, using Git LFS for STEP and GLB? | Your choice. I need a yes or no before the first build. |
| Q-015 | Should the USB-C opening also clear the cable plug's moulded body (usually about 12 × 6.5 mm)? Is the receptacle face flush with the board edge? | Flush receptacle face, and make the opening big enough for the plug body. A 2 mm gap plus a 2 mm wall puts the receptacle 4 mm behind the outside face. |
| Q-016 | Which exact M2.5 and M3 heat-set inserts (supplier and part number)? | Otherwise they stay OPEN, and the boss sizes stay provisional until L2 |
| Q-017 | Do you need vents, LED windows, buttons or rubber feet? | None |
| — | How much documentation: `maker`, `pro` or `regulated`? | `pro` (the template default) |

**Next steps once you answer.** I record your answers and run INTENT, the material and process selection. That needs your approval because it's a single human gate. Then SPECIFY, then L0 concepts: 2–3 variants (for example, a lid that sits on the walls or a lid recessed into them) for you to pick at the VARIANT gate. Then the L1 layout build, its checks, and the LAYOUT freeze gate, which also needs your approval.

Work is paused until you answer.

The LAYOUT freeze is approved on version **v4**, which passed every layout check. The record is now at stage `parts`, so L2 PARTS can start. Two things to know first: the INTENT and VARIANT approvals rest on your standing instruction rather than on you seeing the concepts, and nothing has been committed to git (explained at the end).

## Decisions by stage

| Stage | Outcome | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| GROUND | Use case confirmed: production, 10 end-use units, `maker` rigor, ISO 2768-m general tolerance, generated results kept out of git. Assumptions ASM-001 to ASM-012 recorded. | DR-001, DR-002 |
| INTENT | Selected route: Bambu PETG HF printed on your X1C, with catalogue inserts and screws. PLA and outsourced printing were eliminated because the brief requires PETG on your own X1C. | DR-003, re-confirmed in DR-005 |
| L0 / VARIANT | Three concepts drafted. **A, internal corner columns**, chosen on my recommendation under your instruction. You didn't see the viewer; the viewer is now stopped. | DR-004 |
| L1 LAYOUT | v3's full check failed: the screws were attached to the housing instead of the PCB and lid. I voided that gate, fixed it, and built v4, which passes. | DR-006 provisional, DR-007 void, DR-008 provisional |
| LAYOUT freeze | Approved on v4, recorded only after the full check passed. The sweep-interval acceptance has its own decision record. The enclosure has no movable joints, so no sweep ran and there were no unproved intervals to accept. | DR-009, DR-010 |

## v4 check results

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Record validation | pass, no findings |
| Static check, all 171 part pairs | pass. The only warning is that print orientations are still "proposed"; they get approved at L2. |
| Clearance, component envelope to walls/floor/columns | 2.10 mm (needs ≥ 2.0) |
| Clearance, component envelope to lid | 2.20 mm (needs ≥ 2.0) |
| PCB boss pitch | 72.0 × 42.0 mm |
| USB-C opening | 13.0 × 7.5 mm; fully exposes the 9 × 3.5 mm receptacle |
| Screw thread engagement | M3 5.6 mm, M2.5 4.4 mm (insert length 5.7 mm) |
| Insert holes | 4.0 × 6.7 mm, with 2.1–2.2 mm of wall around them |
| BOM | pass, 7 rows |
| Evidence check for the layout stage | pass |
| Joint sweep and motion render | not applicable (all joints are fixed) |

**Frozen layout:** housing 97.4 × 67.4 × 27.5 mm, 2.4 mm walls, 3.6 mm floor. Flat 2.4 mm lid. Assembled size 97.4 × 67.4 × 29.9 mm.

## Parts to make

| PN | Part | Material | Qty per set |
|---|---|---|---|
| ENC-0001 | Housing | Bambu PETG HF, printed on the X1C | 1 |
| ENC-0002 | Lid | Bambu PETG HF, printed on the X1C | 1 |

## Parts to buy

| PN | Item | Order code | Qty per set |
|---|---|---|---|
| ENC-0003 | Your PCB assembly | OPEN: board part number not given | 1 |
| ENC-0004 | ruthex RX-M2.5x5.7 insert | GE-M25x57-001 | 4 |
| ENC-0005 | ruthex RX-M3x5.7 insert | GE-M3x57-001 | 4 |
| ENC-0006 | M2.5 × 6 button head screw, steel ("ISO 7380-1 style") | OPEN: supplier and steel grade | 4 |
| ENC-0007 | ISO 7380-1 M3 × 8 screw, steel | OPEN: supplier | 4 |

## Assembly order (assumption ASM-005)

1. Heat-set the eight inserts into the housing.
2. Seat the PCB on its four bosses.
3. Drive the four M2.5 screws.
4. Place the lid.
5. Drive the four M3 screws from the top.

## Please confirm before L2

- **ASM-011:** ruthex sells no M2.5 × 4 mm insert, so I used their RX-M2.5x5.7 instead. Also, ISO 7380-1 doesn't cover M2.5 (it starts at M3), so the M2.5 screw can only be "ISO 7380-1 style".
- **ASM-012:** the bosses need component-free circles around each mounting hole: 4.5 mm radius under the board and 3.0 mm on top (room for the screw heads). Please check this against your board layout.
- **ASM-004:** I enlarged the USB-C opening to 13 × 7.5 mm so a cable's moulded plug body can reach the receptacle.
- PETG HF is marked discontinued on the Bambu store.
- Your X1C has no calibration, so actual printed dimensional accuracy is unknown.

## Fix for L2

The assembly steps where inserts sit flush need two reference features each, but name one. This only affects later-stage checks, not the layout gate. Fixing it changes the assembly record, so L2 has to rebuild anyway.

## Not committed to git

The commit check fails because the record is now at stage `parts`, which has no passing check result until L2 is done. Everything is saved on disk but uncommitted. I can commit once L2 passes, or commit the layout state now if you prefer.

The session stops here, as you scoped it, with the LAYOUT freeze decided.

I kept my recommended option on each open item and recorded them as bounded assumptions in a new decision record. Nothing about the frozen v4 layout changed. The record still validates, the selection is still current, and the layout-stage evidence check still passes on v4.

| Item | Kept as |
|---|---|
| ASM-011 | The ruthex RX-M2.5x5.7 insert (order code GE-M25x57-001) replaces the M2.5 × 4 mm insert, which ruthex doesn't sell. The M2.5 × 6 screw stays "ISO 7380-1 style". |
| ASM-012 | Component-free circles around each PCB mounting hole: 4.5 mm radius under the board, 3.0 mm on top. |
| ASM-004 / REQ-009 | The USB-C opening stays 13.0 × 7.5 mm so a cable's moulded plug body fits through. |
| Git commit | Deferred. `hw/` stays on disk, uncommitted, until the first passing PARTS-gate check, then gets one commit. I didn't bypass the pre-commit check. Committing now would mean setting the stage back to `layout`, which would contradict the recorded layout approval. |

All three assumptions stay open in `requirements.yaml` until you confirm them: ASM-011 before ordering, ASM-012 against your board layout, and ASM-004 with your cables on the first printed unit. I tried linking the decision to each assumption inside `requirements.yaml`. That changed the inputs the material and process selection was checked against and made it stale, so I took the links out again; the decision record lists them instead.

These items carry into L2:
- The assembly steps where inserts sit flush need two reference features each.
- Print orientations and supports need approval.
- The X1C has no calibration, so dimensional accuracy is unknown.
- The screw supplier and steel grade are still open.
- PETG HF is discontinued at Bambu.

As scoped, I've stopped after the LAYOUT freeze decision. L2 PARTS can start whenever you're ready.
